title: KV/prefix cache hit-modeling, TTL policy tuning, and cache-key hygiene playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a practical engineering playbook and automation hooks to derive safe KV/prefix caching recommendations for production workloads. Focus areas: (1) offline hit-rate modeling and simulation, (2) TTL and eviction policy tuning with hysteresis windows, and (3) cache-key design patterns that minimize fragmentation and maximize prefix reuse. Deliverables should include a sim harness, config validation rules, an automated canary/rollback workflow, and guidance for when to prefer prefix vs full-key caching.
acceptance_criteria: A hit-rate simulator that ingests 7d production logs and outputs expected hit-rate and cost delta for candidate TTLs and key-normalizations
Automated config validator that rejects unsafe TTL changes (e.g., >10x increase) without an approval flag
Safe rollout automation: staged apply (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with metrics gates and automatic rollback on defined breach conditions
Documentation and checklist for cache-key hygiene (normalization, bucketing, and prefix policies) with examples from two real product routes
Observed cost reduction estimate >8% on at least one representative workload in internal staging using suggested configs
technical_notes: Hit-rate modeling approach: build a per-prefix time-series of requests, compute reuse-distance distribution and simulate TTL effect by computing probability that inter-arrival < TTL for each key bucket
Model inputs: 7 days of request logs, optional user-id affinity metadata, tokenized key canonicalization map (normalizers), and current eviction/size limits
Metric outputs: expected hit-rate, median/worst-case latency delta, token-per-second cost delta, and confidence interval (bootstrap over days)

TTL policy recommendations: use staggered TTLs by prefix class (hot/static/ephemeral). Default candidate rules: hot=60s-300s, warm=300s-3600s, static=>1h. Add TTL hysteresis window: require 24h of stable gain before doubling TTL again
Safety rules: never increase TTL more than 4x in a single rollout and cap max TTL by model memory budget. Reject TTL increases that push estimated on-GPU KV memory > 80% of pool capacity

Cache-key hygiene: prefer prefix bucketing for high-cardinality keys (user-id, session-id). Normalize variable portions (timestamps, UUID fragments) into stable tokens. Example: api.v1.embed.user.{user_id}.{model_version} -> api.v1.embed.user.{user_id % 128}.{model_version} for coarse bucketing
Prefix vs full-key guidance: use prefix cache for deterministic prompt prefixes and repetitive system messages; use full-key for short-lived personalized responses where collision risk is high

Simulation implementation notes: implement in Python using Pandas for aggregation and a Cythonized inner loop for reuse-distance calculation. Provide a fast approximation: exponential inter-arrival fit for prefixes with >10k keys

Observability hooks: instrument per-prefix hit/miss counters, TTL-applied histogram, and estimated memory footprint per prefix. Emit gates as derived SLI: hit-rate delta, median tail latency, and failed-requests increase
Config format: yaml block under runtime.cache.policies with fields: selector (prefix regex), primary_ttl, max_ttl, bucket_fn (mod,N), allow_volatile (true/false), rollout_scale
Validation examples (pseudo): if candidate.primary_ttl > current.primary_ttl * 4 -> require_manual_approval = true; if estimated_memory_pct > 80 -> reject

Prototype hit-rate simulator and run against two internal routes (chat-render and embed-api)
Author config validator and safe-rollout controller (k8s-style 5/25/100 percent steps)
Add observability panels and alerting runbook for rollout gates
Write docs + runbook for cache-key hygiene and distribute to SD and PMs
Run staging experiment and collect cost/latency deltas

rollout_plan: Dry-run: run simulator and validator produce config and expected metrics
Canary-1: apply policy to 5% of traffic for 6 hours. Gate: hit-rate >= simulator_predicted - 2pp OR no increase in error rate >0.5%
Canary-2: 25% for 24 hours if Canay-1 gates pass. Gate: sustained hit-rate improvement and memory <75% capacity
Full: 100% with 48 hour observation. If any gate trips, automatic rollback to previous config
Post-rollout: keep TTL changes immutable for 48h unless manually approved with ops signoff
rollback_procedure: Automated controller will revert runtime.cache.policies to prior config snapshot and scale down applied nodes for 10 minutes to flush transient state. Rollback triggers: hit-rate drop >5 percentage points from baseline, failed-requests increase >1% absolute, or observed KV memory > 85% of pool. On rollback, send incident notification to #runtime-ops with annotated simulation output and raw metrics dump. Manual rollback checklist included in Confluence playbook.
